title: Surge queue & runway checklist — ops log and followups
content:
Purpose:
Quick working log for this week focused on surge queue runway: checklist items, observations from the last dry-run, region-specific constraints, and clear follow-ups. This is an ops-centred doc — notes to be converted into the surge playbook appendix and an action list for the next sprint.

High-level summary:
- Overall fleet headroom: nominally 9% global spare GPU capacity on baseline allocation; effective spare capacity after priority reservations and evacuation buffers ≈ 4.5%.
- Upcoming scheduled events: enterprise demo in APAC on 2028-11-15 likely to add short-lived 14% token spike in hosted API for 2 hours.
- Risk window: 2028-11-14 through 11-16 (demo + model rollout). Need prewarm and priority-band enforcement.

What we ran this week (experiment notes):
1) Priority-band enforcement dry-run (2028-11-07):
   - Goal: ensure low-priority batch jobs are suspended within 45s of the priority signal.
   - Result: median suspension latency = 72s (missed target). Two causes observed: delayed gRPC heartbeat from backfill controller and a throttled kube-apiserver during high control-plane load.
   - Mitigation attempted: temporary bump of controller QPS and small kube-apiserver vertical burst; improvement to median = 38s.
   - Follow-up: add backoff jitter to backfill controller and add metric alert on kube-apiserver request latency.

2) Prewarming microshards for APAC region (2028-11-08):
   - Goal: bring 120 microshards online (model: rwd-llama-7B-q) 10 minutes prior to expected spike.
   - Result: 110 shards provisioned in 8–12 minutes; 10 failed due to missing quantized artifact in S3 mirror apac-eu-mirror-2.
   - Root cause: stale CI artifact promotion step; fixed by re-running promotion job.
   - Note: provisioning variance between machines with NVLink vs without is ~40% for startup time.

Region-specific observations and blockers:
- US-WEST (us-west1):
  - Network egress throttling observed when multiple microshards fetch warmup tokens concurrently. Throttle limit hit at ~1.5 Gbps; resolved by staggering warmup fetches with randomized jitter.
  - Suggested change: introduce a warmup token fetch queue with per-node cap. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2028-11-13.

- EU-CENTRAL (eu-central1):
  - Good spare capacity but intermittent GPU health flaps on node pool gpu-n1. One node returned prolonged ECC warnings yesterday; SRE replaced node and file a hardware ticket with cloud provider.
  - Action: add ECC warning spike to weekly fleet digest and escalate if recurrence within 48h. Owner: Lena. Due: 2028-11-11.

- APAC-SG (apac-sg1):
  - Highest risk for demo. Observed slower prewarm times (see microshard note) and higher teardown variance when capacity reclaimed.
  - Contingency: reserve 8 dedicated microshards pinned to the demo tenant (on dedicated pool) for the demo window. Needs purchase approval for burst reservation. Owner: Omar. Blocker: procurement approval.

Capacity & numbers (current snapshot as of 2028-11-08 09:00 UTC):
- Total GPUs (logical): 14,800
- GPUs allocated to hosted tier: 8,700
- GPUs reserved for dedicated contracts: 4,900
- Spare (unallocated + preemptible candidates): 1,200 (≈8.1% raw spare)
- Effective spare (after evacuation & reservation buffers): 670 (≈4.5%)
- Average token throughput last 24h: 58M tokens/hour; 99th percentile sustained for 10m = 72M tokens/hour

Incidents this week (brief):
- 2028-11-06 03:20 UTC: short-lived routing storm in east-eu causing ~2m of elevated tail latency for hosted API. Root cause: Lambda service reconfiguration pushed incorrectly. Rollback restored normal routing. Action: add pre-deploy routing validation test in CI. Owner: Jae. Due: 2028-11-12.

Operational checklist for the demo window (2028-11-15):
- Pre-demo (T-48h):
  - Confirm artifact promotion to APAC mirror (pass/fail). Owner: Maya. Due: 2028-11-13.
  - Validate reserved microshard purchase/commit with procurement. Owner: Omar. Due: 2028-11-12.
  - Run end-to-end smoke with instrumented latency tracing: 3 calls per model variant. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2028-11-14.
- Pre-demo (T-2h):
  - Trigger prewarm for reserved shards and monitor CPU/GPU temps. Owner: Ravi.
  - Lock capacity routing policy to priority-band mode for demo tenant. Owner: Maya.
- During demo:
  - Keep single SRE on call in #gpu-fleet for fast triage. Owner: Lena (primary), Jae (backup).
  - Run short synthetic load every 15 minutes to ensure consistent latency.
- Post-demo (T+2h):
  - Release reserved shards and run tear-down sanity check. Owner: Omar.
  - Capture a targeted evaluation of output quality under demo load for Optimize team. Owner: Product-Optimize liaison (TBD).

Action items (tracked):
- INFRA-3548: add kube-apiserver request latency alert to ops-metrics. Owner: Lena. Due: 2028-11-11.
- Write small-runbook: "Warmup token fetch queue" with backpressure knobs. Owner: Ravi. Due: 2028-11-13.
- Add pre-deploy routing validation CI job and acanary traffic test. Owner: Jae. Due: 2028-11-12.
- Procurement request for demo-dedicated microshards (8 units) submitted. Owner: Omar. Status: pending.

Open questions / parking lot:
- How long should demo reservations be allowed without explicit billing commitments? Proposal: max 72h hold vs charge after 24h. Need finance guidance.
- Should prewarming fetch tokens be cached in regional S3 with signed short-lived URLs instead of many small requests to central artifact store? Tradeoffs: storage replication cost vs burst egress.
- Is 4.5% effective spare sufficient for peak-day concurrency growth + scheduled rollouts? Consider policy to maintain 7% effective spare for campaign-heavy weeks.

Decisions made this week:
- Agreed to a two-tier warmup: small shared warm pool (best-effort) + dedicated reserved microshards for high-risk demos.
- Priority-band enforcement target tightened to 45s suspension latency; instrumentation and alerts to be added before next rollout.

Notes to convert into playbook appendix:
- Staggered warmup jitter pattern (config snippet): exponential jitter 10–90s, per-node max concurrency 4.
- Prewarm validation checks: artifact checksum, GPU memory post-load confirmation, end-to-end request latency under load.

Meeting attendees (ops huddle 2028-11-08 09:30 UTC):
- Maya Chen (owner), Ravi Patel, Lena García, Omar El-Sayed, Jae Park, SRE on-call (Nora Mills joined briefly).

Next sync: quickops standup 2028-11-11 09:00 UTC to validate infra alerts and procurement status.

If you see anything missing or incorrect, flag here or drop a line in the linked Slack thread.
